newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end higher, feeders set new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end higher, feeders set new highs.

text.p: CME live cattle held firm at the close despite some late profit taking while feeder cattle futures finished up sharply higher at new contract highs.

Live cattle closed 0.700 to 0.200 cent a lb higher with February up 0.650 at 64.925 cents. Distant December and February posted new contract highs. Feeder cattle ended 1.175 to 0.550 higher with March up most at 69.100 cents. All but January feeders set a new contract high with March posting a new high of 69.150 cents.
Commercial and fund buying lifted live cattle early before profit taking pared gains late, traders said.
Buying prompted by cold weather, expected bottoming in the cash beef market and unexpected active packer demand for fed cattle early in the day lifted futures into buy stops.

Packers paid $65 per cwt for cattle Thursday with some of the cattle pulled ahead from next week's showlists in the south and central Plains, at a time when slaughter cattle weights already are well below last year's weights.
"We are seeing a good market, in terms of movement, and this is going to continue to leave feedyards extremely current," said Tom Tippens, CEO of Professional Cattle Consultants Inc.
Tippens noted that cattle weights are still down and he saw evidence beef prices may be low enough to spark retail business.
"The retailer can now see beef as an attractive item to feature in specials," Tippens added.
USDA estimated the average weight of cattle slaughtered under federal inspection last week at 1,163 lbs, down from 1,166 a week earlier and sharply below 1,209 a year earlier.

Strong demand in futures also offset further fund rolling. Cargill Investor Services, Refco, FIMAT Futures USA, Dean Witter and Goldman Sachs were all buying April and selling February, considered mostly to be the "Goldman roll". In live cattle options, trading was active with selling in February 65 and 67 calls and buying of the 65 straddle cited on the runup in futures, pit sources said.
Feeders ran up to new contract highs on early buy stops and remained up sharply late on general demand, traders said.
A strong tone to cash feeders and higher live cattle and lower corn futures combined to boost feeder cattle values. Active fed cattle sales are keeping demand for feeders high.
"We have some seasonal strength - there is demand for feeder cattle after the first of the year," Tippens said.
Friday's grain crop report is expected to show increased corn production. Much of the report is now in the market, traders said.

ADM Investor Services notably bought March while Lind-Waldock lightly sold. E.D.&F. Man was a notable buyer early while Cargill Investor Services spread long August feeders/short December live cattle, pit sources said.
In feeder cattle options, LIT division of First Options bought March 60 puts, pit sources added.
